trim_surface_input_group.description: Rate per LF applies to net trim linear footage from PaintScope. Engine sums all 8 trim component LF inputs and divides by rate to calculate hours. Per PCA P10 one-foot rule: 1 LF of trim (girth < 12 inches) = 1 SF equivalent.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps along building perimeter where landscape is adjacent. SF-based for area coverage. ~14 sec per SF. Includes securing tarps with stakes. Trim protection perimeter is narrower than siding — focused on drip zone below trim, not full wall spray drift.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of plantings within drip/overspray zone. Secure against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage secured at all edges. No gaps.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage secured at all edges. Extended coverage for any spray operations.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay canvas drop cloths and plastic on walkways below trim work area. ~14 sec per SF. Canvas for crew traffic, plastic for overspray.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of walkways within drip zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Canvas on crew traffic areas.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. Taped at all edges. Non-slip surfaces on all traffic areas.

task_production_rates.name: Window Glass Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape masking at casing-to-glass edge + apply masking paper/film over glass pane. ~10 min per window. This spec owns casing-to-glass edge masking (RC-002). Typical window has 4 edges of casing meeting glass — all taped. Film covers full pane.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed at casing edge. No gaps for paint bleed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Tight tape seal at all edges. Film smooth, no wrinkles.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision tape placement. Zero bleed risk. Film taut over full pane.

task_production_rates.name: Door Glass Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape and film mask door glass adjacent to casings. ~12 min per door. Doors are larger panes, often have sidelights — slightly slower than window glass masking.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed at casing edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Tight tape seal. Film smooth and taut.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Precision masking. Zero bleed risk.

task_production_rates.name: Light Fixture Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Bag and tape exterior light fixtures near trim. ~4 min per fixture. Remove cover plate if accessible for cleaner edge.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All fixtures fully masked.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage. Cover plates removed where accessible.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Complete coverage. Cover plates removed. Clean tape lines.

task_production_rates.name: Siding Masking for Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape and plastic along trim-to-siding junction for spray overspray protection. ~1 min per LF. Mask 12-18 inches of siding from trim edge. Required only when application_method = spray. Quantity derived from total trim LF being sprayed.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Siding masked 12 inches from trim edge. Tape tight at junction.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Siding masked 18 inches. Tape tight. Plastic secured.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full siding masking. Tape sealed. No overspray risk.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Equipment & Access Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Set up ladders/scaffold/lift per access type. Stage brushes (angled sash 2.5 in, flat 3 in), paint pots, materials. ~25 min per elevation. Slightly longer than siding brush setup due to more tool variety (two brush types) and multi-component staging.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Access equipment stable. Materials within reach.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Access equipment verified. Fresh brushes staged. Materials pre-mixed.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Equipment verified. Premium brushes. Materials mixed and strained.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Equipment & Access Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Configure airless sprayer with trim tips (211 for narrow boards, 313 for wider), 60-mesh filter, hoses. Set up access. Test pattern on cardboard. ~45 min per elevation.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern verified.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern at correct distance. Backup tips staged.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Equipment calibrated. Multiple test patterns at distance. Backup tips and filters staged.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Wood Trim — Remove Mill Glaze
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand new wood trim with 80-120 grit. Blended rate across all trim component types: fast runs (corner boards ~150 LF/hr narrow), medium runs (fascia/frieze/band ~120 LF/hr), slower detail (casings/sills ~100 LF/hr). Hand blocks for edges and profiles, orbital sander for flat runs. ~30 sec per LF blended.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even scratch pattern. Mill glaze removed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full surface sand. Inspect for missed areas. No glossy patches.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Systematic sanding with inspection. No glossy patches. All profiles reached.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff Sand PVC Trim
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light 220-grit scuff on glossy PVC trim. Faster than wood sanding — just breaking gloss, not removing material. ~24 sec per LF blended. PVC is consistently smooth, no grain variation.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Light scuff. Gloss broken on all surfaces.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform scuff. No glossy patches remaining.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Systematic scuff with inspection under raking light. All surfaces dulled.

task_production_rates.name: Acetone/Alcohol Wipe PVC Cut Edges
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Wipe cut edges of PVC trim with acetone/denatured alcohol. ~20 sec per LF. Not every LF has a cut edge — rate reflects total trim run with proportion of cut edges. Higher effective rate than sanding because acetone wipe is quick contact, not abrasive.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All cut edges wiped.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All cut edges wiped. Verify flash-off before priming.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All cut edges wiped. Flash-off verified. Inspect for residual static dust.

task_production_rates.name: Edge-Seal Composite Trim Field Cuts
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-seal each field-cut edge on composite trim with primer + acrylic latex. ~1 min per cut edge. Includes butt joints, miters, and field cuts. WARRANTY REQUIREMENT — non-negotiable.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Count of field-cut edges on composite trim. Not captured by PaintScope — estimator enters count. Typical: 2-4 cuts per board for butt joints, window/door cutouts, corner returns.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All cut edges sealed. Full coverage. No bare fiber visible.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All cut edges sealed. Inspect for completeness.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All cut edges sealed with double-coat on end grain. Inspect for completeness.

task_production_rates.name: Spot-Prime Tannin Knots (Wood Only)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply alkyd/shellac spot primer on visible knots. ~2 min per knot (locate, brush-apply, feather edges). Includes identifying tannin-rich areas. Rate applies to individual knot count.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Count of visible knots requiring spot-prime on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir). Not captured by PaintScope — estimator enters count based on species and board inspection.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All visible knots spot-primed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All knots spot-primed. Inspect for bleed after drying.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All knots spot-primed. Double-coat large/resinous knots. Inspect for bleed.

task_production_rates.name: Prep Dust Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth dust removal from all trim surfaces after sanding. ~12 sec per LF. Fast pass — tack cloth is contact wipe, compressed air for complex profiles. Trim dust cleanup is faster per LF than siding per SF because trim is narrow and linear.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All sanding dust removed. Surface ready for primer.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All dust removed. Tack cloth verification pass.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Pristine surface. Compressed air for profiles. Tack cloth final pass.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Brush Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply full prime coat to all trim components. Blended rate: fascia/frieze/band 50-60 LF/hr (flat 3-in brush, wider boards), corner boards 60-70 LF/hr (narrow, fast), rake 35-50 LF/hr (angled, elevated), casings 35-50 LF/hr (detail around openings), sills 40-50 LF/hr. Blended ~50 LF/hr. ~72 sec per LF. Brush is primary method — penetrates grain and works into detail profiles.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Primer worked into grain. No holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage. Consistent mil build. No missed areas.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full coverage with systematic inspection. No holidays. Back-brush drips immediately.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray primer on trim. Blended rate: flat trim (fascia/frieze/band) 120-150 LF/hr, detail trim (casings/corners) 80-100 LF/hr. Blended ~100 LF/hr. ~36 sec per LF. Spray is secondary method — used for long continuous runs where masking overhead is justified.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. No runs or sags.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. Inspect for holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect uniformity. Inspect under raking light.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Trim Joints

QT3.notes: Production pace. Clean bead. Tool smooth. ~40 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Careful pace. Consistent bead width. Precision tool smooth. ~48 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Meticulous pace. Perfect bead uniformity. No voids, no overflow. ~60 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply and tool exterior paintable caulk at trim-to-trim joints (corners, miters, butt joints, scarf joints) and trim-to-siding junctions. Rate applies to total trim LF — not all LF has joints, so effective rate is a blended rate representing joint density across all trim components. NEVER caulk window weep holes.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All joints caulked. Smooth tool. Clean edges.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Consistent bead width. Precision tool smooth. Uniform appearance.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect bead uniformity. No voids, no overflow. Invisible joint line.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Window & Door Casing Joints

QT3.notes: Production pace. Clean bead at casing-to-wall junction. ~45 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Careful pace. Consistent bead. ~55 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Meticulous pace. Perfect bead. ~72 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Caulk casing perimeter joints (casing-to-wall/siding). Slightly slower than general trim joints because of detail work around openings and need to avoid weep holes. Input is casing LF only (window + door casing inputs summed).

defect_tolerance.QT3: All casing joints caulked. Clean bead.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Consistent bead. Precision tool smooth.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect bead uniformity. No voids. Weep holes verified clear.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush Application

QT3.notes: Production brush pace. Clean edges. Maintain wet edge. ~72 sec per LF blended.

QT4.notes: Careful brush work. No visible brush marks at 6 ft. ~90 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Meticulous brush work. No visible brush marks at 3 ft. ~120 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-apply first finish coat to all 8 trim components. Blended rate: fascia/frieze/band 50-60 LF/hr (flat brush on wide boards), corner boards 60-80 LF/hr (narrow, fast strokes), rake 30-50 LF/hr (angled work), casings 30-50 LF/hr (detail at glass line), sills 40-60 LF/hr. QT3 base blended ~50 LF/hr. QT4/QT5 progressively slower for tighter tolerance. Brush is primary for trim.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Clean edges. No drips.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage. No brush marks at 6 ft. Clean edges at glass line.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Flawless brush work. No brush marks at 3 ft. Perfect edges.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Application

QT3.notes: Spray finish on trim. Blended flat+detail. ~36 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Slower spray pace. More overlap for consistent mil build. ~42 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Meticulous spray. Multiple light passes. ~51 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray first finish coat. Blended: flat trim (fascia/frieze/band) 120-150 LF/hr, detail trim (casings/corners) 70-100 LF/hr. Blended QT3 base ~100 LF/hr. Spray is secondary method for trim — long runs only. Spray rate must be reasonable vs brush for trim — narrow boards limit spray advantage vs broad wall field.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. No runs, sags, or holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible spray pattern at 3 ft.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect uniformity. No orange peel. Glass-smooth on visible surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Inspection

QT3.notes: Quick scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays. ~7 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Systematic inspection at 6 ft. Mark all visible defects. ~12 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Raking light inspection at 3 ft. Mark every defect on all profiles and edges. ~24 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Inspect first finish coat on all trim components. LF-based inspection is slower per LF than SF-based siding inspection because trim has edges, profiles, and glass-line detail to check. Elevated trim requires binoculars or re-ascending access equipment.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects noted.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All visible defects at 6 ft marked.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Every defect marked. Profiles and edges inspected under raking light.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Sand Between Finish Coats
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light sand between finish coats. QT4: 150 grit light scuff (~24 sec per LF). QT5: 220 grit hand-sand. Blended rate ~150 LF/hr. More detailed than siding intercoat sand because trim has profiles and edges.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Light uniform scuff. Remove nibs and raised grain. No deep scratches.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full hand-sand with 220 grit. Raking light inspection after sanding.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Touch-Up

QT3.notes: Fix obvious defects. Minimal touch-up. ~6 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Fix all found defects. Blend repairs. ~10 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly. No visible repair edges. ~18 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during interstage inspection. Rate reflects defect density per LF of trim — higher tiers find more defects and require more blending.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects repaired.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired and blended at 6 ft.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All defects repaired. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth dust removal after intercoat sanding. ~12 sec per LF. Paired with TSK_XTRM_SAND_INTERCOAT. Same rate as prep dust cleanup.

defect_tolerance.QT4: All sanding dust removed. Surface clean for second finish coat.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Pristine surface. Tack cloth verification. Compressed air for profiles.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush Application

QT3.notes: Same rate as coat 1. Primed/coated surface is consistent. ~72 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Same rate as coat 1. Final appearance coat. ~90 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Same rate as coat 1. Meticulous final coat. ~120 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second (final) finish coat by brush. Same rate as coat 1 — primed/coated surface provides consistent substrate. This is the appearance coat: highest standard of workmanship.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Clean edges. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform. No brush marks at 6 ft. Perfect edges. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Flawless. No brush marks at 3 ft. Perfect edges and transitions. Final coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Application

QT3.notes: Same rate as coat 1 spray. ~36 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Same rate as coat 1. Final appearance coat. ~42 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Same rate as coat 1. Meticulous final coat. ~51 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second (final) finish coat by spray. Same rate as coat 1 — consistent substrate. Final appearance coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Perfect uniformity. Glass-smooth. Final appearance coat.

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection

QT3.notes: Ground-level walkthrough. Scan for obvious defects. ~9 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Ground-level with binoculars for elevated trim. 6 ft viewing standard. ~14 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Comprehensive inspection. Binoculars for elevated. 3 ft standard on accessible. Raking light on primary elevations. ~30 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final walkthrough of all trim components — check coverage, consistency, edge quality at glass line, caulk integrity. All 8 trim component types across all elevations. Elevated trim requires binoculars.

defect_tolerance.QT3: No obvious defects from ground level.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No defects visible at 6 ft. Coverage uniform. Caulk intact.
defect_tolerance.QT5: No defects at 3 ft (accessible) or with binoculars (elevated). Perfect finish.

task_production_rates.name: Final Touch-Up

QT3.notes: Fix noted defects. Minimal touch-up. ~7 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Fix all defects. Blend at 6 ft standard. ~14 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft. ~30 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Rate reflects defect count per LF at each tier — higher tiers find more defects and demand seamless blending.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Noted defects repaired.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended at 6 ft.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended seamlessly at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all protection materials: glass masking tape/film from windows and doors, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, siding masking (if spray). Check glass for tape residue. ~45 min per project. Trim has more protection zones (6) than typical siding (3) — more teardown items. Faster than setup because pull-and-fold vs place-and-secure.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All protection removed. No tape residue.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All removed. Inspect glass for residue. Check landscape for overspray.
defect_tolerance.QT5: All removed. Pristine glass. No overspray on any protected surface.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Equipment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean brushes (water for latex, mineral spirits for alkyd spot primer). If spray: flush airless, clean tips and filters, coil hoses. ~25 min. Brush-only cleanup is ~15 min; spray adds ~10 min.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Brushes cleaned and shaped. Equipment stored.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full clean. Tips and filters inspected.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Full clean. Tips and filters inspected. Equipment ready for next use.

task_production_rates.name: Site Debris Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Collect all debris — sandpaper, caulk tubes, tape, paint cans, acetone containers, used tack cloths. Final site walkthrough. ~20 min.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Site restored. All debris removed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Site restored to pre-work condition.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Site restored. Walkthrough with customer. No evidence of work activity.

factor_modifiers.name: Access Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: General access type modifier for elevation work. Applied to exterior trim tasks that involve working at height. This is the base exterior access modifier — trim-specific height tiers (FAC_XTRM_HEIGHT_TIER) provide more granular height-based adjustment for production tasks.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied to protection/setup/teardown tasks where access type affects pace. Production tasks (sand, prime, finish) use FAC_XTRM_HEIGHT_TIER instead for more precise height-based scaling.

factor_modifiers.name: Exterior Trim Height Tier Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Trim-specific height modifier tiers. More aggressive than general FAC_EXT_ACCESS because trim requires fine brush detail at height — precise brush strokes, maintaining wet edge, working from ladders/scaffold with limited reach.
factor_modifiers.notes: Per Exterior_Trim_Systems_Doctrine.md section 4. More aggressive than general access modifier because trim requires fine brush detail at height. Ground = first floor trim. 8ft = upper first floor and lower second floor trim. 13ft = upper second floor fascia/rake. 17ft = gable peak and high dormers. 19ft = tall three-story fascia/rake. Most residential exterior trim falls in ground to 13ft range.

factor_modifiers.name: Profile Complexity Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Built-up or crown trim profiles require more time per LF due to multiple surfaces, inside corners of the profile, and more precise brush work.
factor_modifiers.notes: Standard = flat stock, single-piece trim (most NC). Crown = single-piece crown molding profile with curved face. Built_up = multi-piece cornice assemblies (stacked crown + flat + bed mold). Typically affects fascia/frieze area. Standard profile is most common in NC.

factor_modifiers.name: Quality Tier Base Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Quality tier affects pace on binary tasks that do not have explicit qt_rates. Higher tier = slower pace, more thorough execution.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied to binary tasks where quality tier affects pace but not process steps. Qt_scaled tasks already have per-tier rates and should NOT have this modifier applied (double-counting). QT3 is baseline. QT4 adds 15% time for more thorough execution. QT5 adds 30% for meticulous execution.

factor_modifiers.name: Substrate Material Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Substrate material affects production rate on coating tasks. PVC is slightly slower due to different coating behavior (less absorption, more prone to runs on non-porous surface).
factor_modifiers.notes: Wood and composite have similar coating behavior (absorptive substrates). PVC is non-porous — paint sits on surface, more prone to runs and sags. 10% time increase accounts for slower brush pace needed on PVC to prevent runs.

factor_modifiers.name: Wind Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wind affects exterior trim production — spray operations blocked in high wind (per site_condition_rules), brush operations slowed by wind-blown debris and accelerated drying.
factor_modifiers.notes: Spray tasks have hard block in high wind per site_condition_rules — not included in spray task modifier list. Brush tasks are possible in high wind but significantly slower due to debris contamination, accelerated dry time (shorter wet edge), and crew discomfort. Caulk application also affected — wind draws caulk bead away.

factor_modifiers.name: Sun Exposure Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Full sun exposure forces earlier scheduling, reduces daily productive hours, and accelerates drying (shorter wet edge).
factor_modifiers.notes: Full sun accelerates drying — shorter wet edge window requires faster brush pace or smaller sections. Painter must chase shade around building. Affects scheduling more than rate, but rate impact is real.

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Temperature Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Extreme surface temperatures affect coating application and extend recoat intervals.
factor_modifiers.notes: Cold (below 50F) slows drying, extends recoat wait, forces smaller sections to maintain wet edge. Hot (above 90F) accelerates drying, increases risk of lap marks, may force early morning scheduling. Normal = 50-90F range.

factor_modifiers.name: Substrate Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Substrate condition affects prep task rates. NC trim is typically clean/new, but site conditions may introduce dust, construction debris, or minor damage.
factor_modifiers.notes: NC trim is usually clean and new (baseline). Dusty: construction site dust accumulation requires extra cleaning before sanding. Minor damage: dents, scuffs from installation require additional spot prep.

quality_effects.notes: Standard tier for NC exterior trim. 1 prime + 2 finish coats. Interstage inspection but no sanding. 6 ft viewing standard from ground.
Premium tier. 1 prime + 2 finish coats. Light sand between coats (150 grit). Systematic inspection at 6 ft. Binoculars for elevated trim. Premium acrylic-urethane finish.
Superior tier. 1 prime + 2 finish coats. Hand-sand between coats (220 grit) with raking light inspection. 3 ft standard on accessible trim, binoculars for elevated. Premium acrylic-urethane finish.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Ground-level corner boards, standard profile, wood — baseline
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case — ground level, standard flat trim, wood substrate.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Second-story fascia (13 ft), built-up cornice, PVC substrate
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: High but within 4.0x stacking cap. Built-up cornice at second story on PVC is demanding but manageable.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Gable peak rake (17 ft), crown profile, PVC, QT5
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: QT5 base rate already lower (30 LF/hr). Combined modifiers under cap. ~11 LF/hr effective — very slow but realistic for detailed brush work at gable peak.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Maximum stack — 19 ft, built-up, PVC, QT5, full sun, moderate wind
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: EXCEEDS 4.0x stacking cap (5.57x). Flag for review — recommend hourly billing or breaking job into phases. This extreme combination is rare but possible on tall custom homes.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Typical residential — first floor casings, ground, standard, wood, QT3
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Most common residential scenario. Ground-level window/door casings. ~50 LF/hr brush — reasonable production.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Common residential — second floor trim (8 ft height), standard, wood, QT3
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Very common — upper first floor / lower second floor trim from 8ft ladder. ~38.5 LF/hr — reasonable.

assumptions: Base rates are blended across all 8 trim component types at ground access on standard flat profile with wood substrate.
Individual component rates vary: corner boards fastest (narrow), casings/sills/rake slowest (detail work, angles). Blended rate represents typical residential trim mix.
Height tier, profile complexity, and substrate modifiers stack multiplicatively: effective_rate = base_rate / (height x profile x substrate).
Modifier stacking cap: 4.0x maximum combined. Combinations exceeding 4.0x should be flagged for hourly billing.
Spray rates are secondary — spray is only used for long continuous runs (fascia, frieze, band) where masking overhead is justified by production speed.
PCA P10 one-foot rule: all LF-based rates assume trim girth < 12 inches. For boards wider than 12 inches, rates should be reduced proportionally.
Environmental conditions (wind, sun, surface temp) ARE estimation modifiers for exterior trim, unlike fiber cement siding (where they were excluded per RC-003).
Caulk rates are qt_scaled because higher quality tiers demand more precise bead control and tooling.
Brush prime rate (50 LF/hr) is set as binary because primer is applied consistently regardless of quality tier — primer is hidden under finish coats.
FIXED time tasks (equipment setup, protection teardown, cleaning, site cleanup) are per-elevation or per-session — not per LF.
Protection teardown is FIXED (45 min) rather than LF-based because trim has 6 protection zones to tear down — zone count matters more than trim footage.
risks: Maximum modifier stacking (19ft + built_up + PVC + full sun + wind) exceeds 4.0x cap (5.57x) — recommend hourly billing for this extreme combination.
Glass masking rate (6 EA/hr windows, 5 EA/hr doors) assumes standard rectangular openings — specialty shapes (arched, octagonal) are significantly slower.
Composite edge-seal rate (60 EA/hr) is estimated from sibling FC siding spec — needs field calibration on trim-specific cut profiles.
Knot spot-prime rate (30 EA/hr) depends heavily on knot density which varies by species and board selection — cedar can have 3-5x more knots than pine.
Caulk casing rate is separate from general trim joint caulk — engine must avoid double-counting casing LF across both caulk tasks.
Spray rates do not include masking time — masking is a separate task (TSK_XTRM_SIDING_MASK_SPRAY). Effective spray throughput must account for masking overhead.
Wind blocks spray operations entirely (site_condition_rules) — estimator must have brush fallback plan for weather variability.
validation_plan: Time 3 brush finish projects on standard residential trim at ground level to calibrate baseline 50 LF/hr.
Compare brush rates across component types: fascia vs casing vs corner board — validate blended rate assumption.
Time 2 spray projects on long-run fascia/frieze to validate 100 LF/hr spray baseline.
Track glass masking time per window/door to validate 6 EA/hr and 5 EA/hr rates.
